name: PS1 look (vertex snap, affine textures, low-res dither, blink and dread effects)
what: Draws a three.js scene like a PlayStation 1 game: 320 x 240 with a 4:3 letterbox, vertices snapped to the pixel grid, affine (warping) textures on normal lit materials, 20 colour levels with 4x4 Bayer dither, a green-sepia horror grade, grain and vignette. Also has eyes-closed blackout with a fading afterimage, eyelids, flash, chunky shake, a vignette punch and 'dread' (swimming rows, colour split). Includes eight tiny procedural textures.
use_when: the game wants a retro PS1 / PSX, low-poly 90s 3D or lo-fi horror look, or blink / eyes-closed / jump-scare screen effects
good_for: Retro 3D and horror games, first-person exploration, anything built from simple low-poly shapes and tiny textures; converting the starter's meshes in one line with patchPS1Material. Cheap: the scene is drawn at 320 x 240.
not_for: Smooth modern or painterly looks, 2D pixel art (use pixelfx or meticulai-pixel-3d), WebGPU games, or scenes with huge unsubdivided floors (affine warp tears them).
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-ps1-look, then replace renderer.render with PS1Pipeline.render and patch materials (HOW-TO-USE.md)
